Here’s a highly advanced Keras project that’s significantly different—and more advanced—than typical supervised tasks: we’re diving into self-supervised contrastive learning using SimCLR. It’s a full implementation with encoder, projection head, NT‑Xent loss, and linear probing.

Project Title

Self‑Supervised Contrastive Learning with Keras (SimCLR)
simclr_contrastive_learning.py

Short Description:
Leverage unlabeled data to learn powerful image embeddings via contrastive learning (SimCLR), then evaluate quality via linear probing on downstream classification. This project demonstrates deep self-supervised representation learning using Keras (Keras).

Problem Domain

Computer Vision — Representation Learning via contrastive self-supervision.

Frameworks

  • TensorFlow/Keras
  • tf.data & tf.keras.layers

🧠 Python Code (majority)

# simclr_contrastive_learning.py
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import numpy as np

# Hyperparameters
batch_size: int = 256
img_size: int = 32
proj_dim: int = 128
temperature: float = 0.5
epochs: int = 50

# NT-Xent (InfoNCE) Loss
def nt_xent_loss(proj_1: tf.Tensor, proj_2: tf.Tensor, temperature: float) -> tf.Tensor:
    z = tf.concat([proj_1, proj_2], axis=0)
    z = tf.math.l2_normalize(z, axis=1)
    logits = tf.matmul(z, z, transpose_b=True) / temperature
    n = tf.shape(proj_1)[0]
    labels = tf.concat([tf.range(n, 2*n), tf.range(0, n)], axis=0)
    return keras.losses.sparse_categorical_crossentropy(labels, logits, from_logits=True)

# Data augmentation pipeline
augmenter = keras.Sequential([
    layers.RandomFlip("horizontal"),
    layers.RandomCrop(img_size, img_size),
    layers.RandomContrast(0.5),
])

# Encoder + projection head
def get_simclr_model():
    base = keras.applications.ResNet50(weights=None, include_top=False, input_shape=(img_size, img_size, 3))
    pool = layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D()(base.output)
    proj = layers.Dense(256, activation='relu')(pool)
    proj = layers.Dense(proj_dim)(proj)
    return keras.Model(inputs=base.input, outputs=proj, name="simclr_model")

model = get_simclr_model()

opt = keras.optimizers.Adam()

# Contrastive training loop
@tf.function
def train_step(x):
    x1 = augmenter(x, training=True)
    x2 = augmenter(x, training=True)
    with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
        z1 = model(x1, training=True)
        z2 = model(x2, training=True)
        loss = tf.reduce_mean(nt_xent_loss(z1, z2, temperature))
    grads = tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_variables)
    opt.apply_gradients(zip(grads, model.trainable_variables))
    return loss

# Dataset
(ds_train, ds_val), _ = keras.datasets.cifar10.load_data()
ds_train = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(ds_train).map(lambda x, y=None: tf.cast(x, tf.float32)/255.0).shuffle(10000).batch(batch_size)

# Training loop
for epoch in range(epochs):
    total_loss = 0.0
    for step, batch in enumerate(ds_train):
        loss = train_step(batch)
        total_loss += loss
    print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{epochs}, loss={total_loss/(step+1):.4f}")

# Linear evaluation
features = model.layers[-3].output  # pre-projection
linear_model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.Input(shape=features.shape[1:]),
    layers.Dense(10)
])
linear_model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])
# Prepare frozen encoder + features extraction
encoder = keras.Model(model.input, features)
train_feats = encoder.predict(ds_train.map(lambda x: x))
train_labels = np.concatenate([y for x, y in ds_train])
linear_model.fit(train_feats, train_labels, epochs=20, validation_split=0.1)

📊 Example Use Case

# Example inference
img: tf.Tensor = tf.random.uniform((1, img_size, img_size, 3))
feat: tf.Tensor = encoder(img)
# feat is a 2048‑dim vector; can be used for k‑NN, clustering, transfer tasks
